newsitem.title: UK: Base metals end higher, zinc near 4-1/2 year high.
newsitem.headline: Base metals end higher, zinc near 4-1/2 year high.

text.p: Short-covering helped to lift base metals by the close of London Metal Exchange business on Thursday, a move that may spark further gains near-term if overhead resistance levels are breached.
Zinc probed 4-1/2 year lows, nickel found support from a strike at Inco, while aluminium clawed towards the $1,600 level.

Investment fund buying and short-covering after a recent corrective pull back propelled zinc higher. Traders said the market was gaining in upside confidence after expected Chinese deliveries into LME warehouses failed to materialise.
Several traders recently have said they had heard that around 30,000 tonnes of zinc was on the way to Singapore warehouses.

Martin Squires of LME brokers Rudolf Wolff said the lack of deliveries and a change in chart signals looked fairly constructive to upside gains in the market. But, like others, Squires said a lot depended on near-term stock moves.
"The Chinese may be tempted to move material as prices strengthen," one trader said.
"A break above the $1,379/80 level suggests further strength," Squires said referring to the markets chart outlook.
Last zinc business was at $1,375, a $25 gain from Wednesday's close.

The strike at Inco Sudbury continued to underpin nickel which finished $40 higher at $7,240. Traders said they will closely monitor the developments at Inco after several metal analyst have said they expect the dispute to be long drawn out.
Traders noted news that gas supplies at Norilsk nickel main production complex have been cut by nearly one third.
This could possibly force a cut in nickel production.
Aluminium moved to test $1,600, though overhead selling was capping further gains up to resistance placed at $1,610 and $1,620.
Traders said they expected the market to consolidate after recent LME stock falls. They are expecting a further decline on Friday.
Copper remained quiet and was last at $2,481, up $3.
Martin Squires said the market was finding it difficult to establish upside momentum following recent market talk of Chinese liquidation.
Lead moved higher with zinc to $12 higher at $638. Tin was quiet and last at $5,670, up $70 following trade buying and short-covering.
Alloy was quoted at $1,480/85, unchanged. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542-8075
